newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans mostly down on spreads, weak cash.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans mostly down on spreads, weak cash.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures were mostly lower at midsession Tuesday as July continued to come under pressure from profit-taking on the new crop/old crop spread, traders said.
"The commercials are active in the spread again today," said one floor trader. "They're getting out of it."
Weakness in soybean cash markets also contributed to the weak tone in July soybeans, traders said. Several commercial firms are now quoting bids basis CBOT August or November instead of July.
As a result, some cash soybean prices were weaker Tuesday.
New crop months were supported by forecasts showing cooler-than-normal temperatures in the Midwest.

The National Weather Service's latest 6- to 10-day forecast indicated below-normal tempertures for much of the Midwest. The cool weather has led to ongoing concerns about emergence and growth rates in the newly planted crops.
In early trade, ADM and O'Connor Grain each sold one million bushels of November. FIMAT Futures, Inc. bought 1.5 million November, and Prudential sold one million July.
At 1112 CDT, CBOT soybeans were two cents per bushel higher to 6-3/4 cents lower with July down 6-3/4 at $8.68-1/2.
